title: The evidence index, the agent tools and the blind leakage-auditor replay
request: Make all the R&D data usable in practice now, without fine-tuning: say how evidence should be shaped for retrieval, build it, and give an agent tools to use it. Then check that the agent's leakage tool would find the leaks the R&D already confirmed without being told.
spec: dclab_rnd/evidence_index.py: every rule, workflow block, dataset, experiment, leakage precedent, pitfall and finding as one self-contained cited record (evidence/knowledge/rag/records.jsonl), searched filter-first then ranked; a freshness check in CI. dclab_rnd/tools.py: search_evidence, get_record, plan_next_stage, review_notebook, review_code and audit_columns for function calling or MCP. A blind replay of the column auditor with no catalog and no precedents (agent_verification_v1).
plan: Shape records, not chunks: a rule keeps its statement, why and failure signal together; an experiment card always says what the dataset predicts and what the stage does.
Search with exact metadata filters first (type, dataset, stage, task type, category), then rank the survivors with a small BM25.
Expose the index and the deterministic checks as tools with JSON schemas.
Run the column auditor blind on every dataset with a confirmed leak and compare its flags with the known leaks.
Rebuild the index when the expansion campaign lands and rerun the replay on its datasets.

decisions.decision: Filter first, rank second; never chunk records like a PDF.
decisions.why: A question almost always names its dataset or stage, so an exact filter is free and precise; chunking would separate a rule's statement from its reason.

decisions.decision: Keep the index in the standard library and deterministic.
decisions.why: CI can then verify that the committed records are current, and BM25 can be swapped for embeddings later without changing the record contract.

decisions.decision: Use the blind replay as the auditor's regression test.
decisions.why: Any change to its heuristics must not lower recall on leaks the R&D already confirmed.

change: dclab_rnd/evidence_index.py (build, check, search), dclab_rnd/tools.py with six tools and a verify-auditor command, evidence/knowledge/rag/records.jsonl, evidence/campaigns/agent_verification_v1/VERIFICATION_REPORT.md, tests/test_knowledge_layer.py and docs/guides/AGENT_KNOWLEDGE_ARCHITECTURE.md.

findings.defect: The evidence index and the SFT corpus went stale when the expansion results were added.
findings.scenario: After the 20 expansion results landed, tests/test_knowledge_layer.py failed its freshness checks for the index and the corpus.
findings.cause: Generated files were not rebuilt after new results.
findings.fix: Rebuild with python -m dclab_rnd.evidence_index build and the v3 builder (make knowledge); rd-check fails while either is stale.
findings.impact: Until the rebuild, search_evidence answered without the 20 expansion experiments (no fraud, multiclass, time-series or text evidence) and SFT v3 would have trained without them, while both files looked current.
findings.open: Freshness is checked, not automatic: after new results someone still has to run make knowledge, and rd-check fails until they do.

measurements.name: blind leakage-auditor replay
measurements.gate: Run the auditor with blind=True (no catalog, no precedents) on 7 datasets with 18 confirmed leakage columns; count the leaks it flags.
measurements.result: 11 of 18 found (recall 61%): bank duration; online_shoppers 4 of 9 (PageValues and the three duration columns; missed Administrative, Informational, ProductRelated, BounceRates, ExitRates); both HyperAck final fares; Telco customerID; credit-card fraud's Time missed; bike casual and registered; reviews Rating found, Positive Feedback Count missed. Other flags (review requests, not accusations) included TotalCharges and HyperAck's first_created_at.
measurements.next: Never treat a clean heuristic scan as proof of safety; the agent must ask for the decision-time contract.
measurements.against_gate: There is no pass mark: run blind on 7 datasets, the auditor found 11 of the 18 confirmed leaks (recall 61%). It found every leak on bank, HyperAck, Telco and bike, 4 of 9 on online_shoppers and Rating but not Positive Feedback Count on the reviews, and it missed credit-card fraud's Time.
limits: Eighteen known leaks across seven datasets is a small set; recall of 61% could move a lot with a few more cases.
Only recall was measured; the other flags (TotalCharges, first_created_at) are review requests, and precision was not scored.
The heuristics were written by people who knew these datasets, so this is a regression test, not a blind estimate on new data.
The missed leaks look like ordinary numbers; no column heuristic can find them, so the gap is structural rather than a matter of tuning.

outcome: 133 cited records at the time (137 later) searchable by dataset and stage, six agent tools, and a regression test for the leakage auditor. The MCP path was not exercised in that environment because the mcp package was missing.
lessons: A missed leak is one whose numbers look ordinary; only the moment a value is written can catch it.
Shape knowledge for its reader: a record that cannot be understood alone is useless to retrieval and to training alike.
risks: Chunking records like documents, so a rule's statement is separated from its reason and its failure signal.
An index that silently goes stale when new results land.
Tools that let an agent present a clean heuristic leakage scan as proof that the data is safe.
Measuring the auditor with the catalog or the precedents switched on, so it finds the leaks it was told about.
Shipping an MCP path that was never exercised because the mcp package is missing.
